A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SANTA study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original kernel timings, GSM8K, MMLU and RULER evaluations, numerical experiments, layer ablations, and learned sampling-budget results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds LongBench v2, HumanEval, end-to-end decoding measurements, and kernel-fidelity analyses.

M1.justification: The sampling rules, prop/flash kernels, Bernoulli query sampling, mean-group-query estimator, and reinforcement-learning budget allocation are retained. Algorithms 1–8 are unchanged. Section 3 adds an explanation of the kernels' relationship to systematic sampling, not a procedural revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds LongBench v2 long-context reasoning evaluations (Section 3.4 and Appendix I) and HumanEval code generation (Appendix T). These substantially broaden task coverage beyond the retained GSM8K, MMLU, and RULER evaluations.

E2.justification: The existing SDPA, top-k, FlashInfer, and FlashDecoding comparisons are retained. FlashAttention-2, used for the new end-to-end comparison, already appears as FlashDecoding in v1's microbenchmark. LongBench v2 and HumanEval reuse SDPA; ShadowKV, OmniKV, and DuoAttention are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include batched generation with six 30k-token prompts and 2048 generated tokens, HumanEval greedy pass@1 evaluation, and controlled fidelity measurements over 40 prompts per task and 32 decoding steps. LongBench v2 introduces 32k truncation. The stated microbenchmark flash-attn version also changes from 2.7.3 to 2.7.1, without establishing that retained timings were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix U adds controlled comparisons of sparse and dense outputs at identical decode states, attention-support analysis across tiles, and a tile-size sweep. Tables 28–30 investigate approximation errors and failure conditions beyond the retained variance, one-hot-layer, and learned-budget analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds repetition and aggregation specifications for new experiments: three LongBench v2 runs and end-to-end timing averages over nine batches. The existing 95% bootstrap-CI practice and retained experiments' repetition information remain unchanged; no increase in runs for existing results is established.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. New Table 3 reports decode times of 101.22 seconds per batch for FlashAttn-2, 80.97 for S2ANTA-flash, and 82.36 for S2ANTA-prop, yielding 1.250x and 1.229x speedups. LongBench v2, HumanEval, and fidelity/sensitivity tables add substantial new outcomes rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The estimator definitions, unbiasedness and variance proofs, Bernstein bound, and operation-count analyses are retained. Section 3.5 adds a limited quantitative bandwidth-model calculation: approximately 15 GB of weight traffic and 24 GB of KV traffic, combined with a 1.5x kernel gain, predict a 1.26x decode speedup. v1 only discussed the Amdahl constraint qualitatively.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion extend the central efficiency claim from attention-kernel acceleration to measured full-model decode-latency acceleration of up to 1.25x in batched generation. The original sampling and kernel-speedup claims remain, but the claimed practical benefit now covers a substantially broader execution scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 develops explanations of bandwidth shares and how batching, context length, weight quantization, and KV quantization affect benefits. Section 6 qualifies untested cache-method combinations and MLA applicability. Appendix U adds interpretations of diffuse attention and small tiles as sources of approximation error, motivating future tile-aware allocation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new generation configuration, LongBench truncation, HumanEval grading, and fidelity-measurement procedure. Appendix R revises the reported flash-attn version from 2.7.3 to 2.7.1. Existing kernel pseudocode, detailed microbenchmark instructions, and repository access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 extends the existing complementarity argument through discussion of ShadowKV, OmniKV, DuoAttention, MLA/DeepSeek-V2, and stochastic spiking attention. References for LongBench v2, HumanEval, and FlashAttention-2 are also added. The overall positioning as value-stage sparsification complementary to cache management remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract, conclusion, and Section 4 introduction, clarifies kernel terminology, standardizes headings, and adds acknowledgments and conference publication text. References move before the appendices. Most existing exposition and the overall method-to-evaluation structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Seven new tables provide LongBench summaries and sweeps, end-to-end timings, HumanEval results, and three fidelity/sensitivity displays (Tables 2, 3, 18, and 27–30). This substantially expands the displayed evidence. Existing Figures 1–10 are retained, while existing tables and figures are repositioned through page reflow.

improvement.justification: v1 demonstrated kernel acceleration without measuring full-model decode savings. v2 closes that important validation gap with Table 3's batched decode measurements, reporting prefill separately. LongBench v2 and HumanEval broaden accuracy evidence, while Appendix U identifies conditions affecting kernel fidelity. Together these substantially strengthen practical validation and applicability guidance, although measured speedups remain limited to Llama 8B on RTX 6000 Ada.
